objective: Repair the CBFS field-inversion objective -- restore the benchmark's own inlet profile that the patchV pilot overwrote -- then re-baseline and re-run the Stage 1 inversion with the existing out-of-process driver
rationale: The Stage 1 CBFS inversion (s1-cbfs-field-inversion-run, 335.98 core-min) failed both pre-registered gates for a measured reason: the case's 0/U inlet is Ux=0.72 uniform (the patchVelocity pilot's write-back; the benchmark ships a developed profile, bulk 0.9149, and the identical Uz noise columns prove the overwrite), so the varianceU loss carries a 27 percent bulk mass-flux mismatch against the Bentaleb LES reference that no interior beta can remove -- 85.1 percent of the loss sits at y>2 in trivially-matched channel flow and only 3.7 percent in the separated-flow window. The inversion machinery itself worked end to end (17 converged adjoints, gradient norm down 106x, bit-identical controls). Plan: (1) restore the benchmark clone's inlet boundaryField into the case and re-verify the FD gate at one cell under the corrected objective; (2) re-baseline varianceU -- PREDICTION, stated before the run: the beta=1 objective falls by well over half once the inlet matches the reference bulk; (3) re-run the existing driver unchanged, with a Wu/Zhang-style sparse-point separation-region loss as the pre-registered variant and lambda_L2 re-tuned and disclosed. The destruction-term patch (w3-beta-on-omega-destruction-model-patch, spec ready) is the term-parity follow-on after this repair; a Dow-style nu_t-discrepancy parameterization is the named alternative if the measured 49.5 percent limiter-binding overlap on the top-decile beta cells caps what the production hook can reach.
cost_basis: measured: 16.4 core-min per evaluation (cold compute_totals, W4 twice, reconfirmed 17 times by s1-cbfs-field-inversion-run at --cpus=2); one FD-gate check ~35 core-min; re-baseline ~9; leaves ~24 evaluations
gate: Pre-registration first, as before. FD gate at one cell under the corrected objective to the W4 order; the re-baseline prediction graded; then the inversion's own pre-registered J-reduction and beta-locality gates, set after the corrected baseline is known
expected_knowledge_gain: Whether a production-term beta can actually move a well-posed CBFS velocity loss -- the question the defective objective masked -- and the corrected foundation Stage 2 needs
